title: Equivalences over the interval preserve and reflect cocartesian edges
statement: Use small quasicategories, functor equivalences and simplicial pullbacks of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], inner fibrations and cocartesian edges of [def-coef-infinity-fibrations], and categorical equivalences of [lem-coef-joyal-model-structure]. Let $p:E\to\Delta^1$ and $q:F\to\Delta^1$ be inner fibrations between quasicategories. Let $v:E\to F$ be a simplicial map with $qv=p$, and suppose its underlying map is a categorical equivalence. For every edge $u$ of $E$, $u$ is $p$-cocartesian if and only if $v(u)$ is $q$-cocartesian. No cocartesian lifts of all base edges, fibration hypothesis on $v$, or quasi-inverse strictly over $\Delta^1$ is assumed.

source.place: Higher Algebra, Lemma B.2.4(a), printed pp.1483-1484: invariance of local cocartesianness under equivalence on edge pullbacks. Read online 2026-10-17; not archived in literature/. No Stacks tag states this quasicategorical fact.

proof.text: First extract an underlying coherent inverse, without imposing a condition over the base. By [lem-coef-joyal-functor-equivalence-test], precomposition by $v$ induces equivalences on the ordinary homotopy categories of functors into $E$ and into $F$. Essential surjectivity for target $E$ gives $w:F\to E$ and an isomorphism $wv\cong1_E$ in $h\operatorname{Fun}(E,E)$. Postcompose this isomorphism by $v$, obtaining $vwv\cong v$. Full faithfulness of precomposition for target $F$ lifts that isomorphism, and its inverse, to an isomorphism $vw\cong1_F$ in $h\operatorname{Fun}(F,F)$: the inverse equations follow by faithfulness. The functor simplicial sets are quasicategories by the same cited theorem. Apply [lem-coef-quasicategory-invertible-interval] to these two functor quasicategories; each isomorphism is represented by a $J$-path. Its forward and reverse edges and inverse triangles give coherent natural equivalences $wv\simeq1_E$ and $vw\simeq1_F$, in the sense of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Thus $v$ is a functor equivalence.

source.place: Lemma B.2.4, proof (a), printed pp.1483-1484; agent expansion: categorical equivalence versus coherent inverse

proof.text: By [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus], the functor equivalence just constructed gives weak homotopy equivalences $\operatorname{Map}_E(a,b)\to\operatorname{Map}_F(va,vb)$ for all vertices $a,b$. The same node says that the components of the coherent natural equivalence $vw\simeq1_F$ are equivalence edges. Consequently for every vertex $z\in F$ there is a vertex $t=wz\in E$ and an equivalence edge $e:vt\to z$. These statements supply precisely full faithfulness and essential surjectivity needed below.

source.place: Lemma B.2.4, proof (a), printed pp.1483-1484; agent expansion: mapping spaces and image objects

proof.text: Compute the base mapping spaces directly from [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. For $i,j\in\{0,1\}$, an $n$-simplex of $\operatorname{Map}_{\Delta^1}(i,j)$ is a monotone map $[n+1]\to[1]$ with the first $n+1$ vertices all $i$ and the last vertex $j$. There is exactly one if $i\leq j$ and none otherwise. Thus this mapping space is respectively $*$ or $\varnothing$, degreewise. For any simplicial map $r:C\to\Delta^1$, applying $r$ to a right-pinched simplex gives a map $\operatorname{Map}_C(a,b)\to\operatorname{Map}_{\Delta^1}(ra,rb)$. In particular $ra>rb$ forces $\operatorname{Map}_C(a,b)=\varnothing$.

source.place: Lemma B.2.4, proof (a), printed pp.1483-1484; agent expansion: explicit point-or-empty calculation for the interval

proof.text: Fix $u:x\to y$ and put $i=p(x)\leq j=p(y)$. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-mapping-criterion] to $p$. For a test vertex $t$ with $k=p(t)$, if $j\leq k$ both bottom corners of its square are $*$. Its path homotopy pullback is then exactly $\operatorname{Map}_E(x,t)$, so the square is a homotopy pullback exactly when $u^*:\operatorname{Map}_E(y,t)\to\operatorname{Map}_E(x,t)$ is a weak homotopy equivalence. If $j>k$, its bottom left corner and its upper left corner are both empty by step 3. The path homotopy pullback is empty as well, so the comparison is the identity of the empty space. Therefore $u$ is $p$-cocartesian exactly when $u^*$ is a weak homotopy equivalence for every $t$ with $p(t)\geq j$. The identical calculation for the inner fibration $q$ characterizes $q$-cocartesianness of $v(u)$ by the same test on all $z\in F$ with $q(z)\geq j$. The inner-fibration and quasicategory hypotheses required by the criterion are exactly the hypotheses of the item.

source.place: Lemma B.2.4, proof (a), printed pp.1483-1484; agent expansion: apply the general mapping-square criterion and evaluate its path pullbacks

proof.text:
For each vertex $t\in E$, functoriality of Hom [lem-coef-infinity-hom-bifunctor-functoriality], applied to $v$ and to the edge $u$ in its first variable, supplies the homotopy-commuting square
$$\begin{array}{ccc}\operatorname{Map}_E(y,t)&\xrightarrow{u^*}&\operatorname{Map}_E(x,t)\\
\downarrow v_*&&\downarrow v_*\\
\operatorname{Map}_F(vy,vt)&\xrightarrow{v(u)^*}&\operatorname{Map}_F(vx,vt).\end{array}$$
Both vertical maps are weak homotopy equivalences by step 2. Hence the upper arrow is a weak homotopy equivalence if and only if the lower arrow is: apply the square on components and on each based homotopy group. A homotopy changes a basepoint only by the corresponding path, giving a conjugate isomorphism, so strict commutation is unnecessary. Notice also $q(vt)=p(t)$ from $qv=p$. This compares precisely the tests in step 4 at image objects.

source.place: Lemma B.2.4, proof (a), printed pp.1483-1484; agent expansion: compare precomposition at the image targets

proof.text:
For an arbitrary $z\in F$, take $e:vt\to z$ as in step 2 and choose its inverse edge $e':z\to vt$ with inverse triangles. Applying $q$ to those triangles gives inverse edges in $\Delta^1$. Since its only invertible edges are identities, $q(vt)=q(z)$. By the associativity, unit, component-dependence and inverse-triangle assertions of [lem-coef-infinity-mapping-composition], postcomposition by $e$ on $\operatorname{Map}_F(vy,vt)$ and on $\operatorname{Map}_F(vx,vt)$ has postcomposition by $e'$ as homotopy inverse: the two composites are homotopic to postcomposition by an identity. They are weak homotopy equivalences by [lem-cbc-simplicial-homotopy-equivalence-weak]. The same associativity identifies
$$e_*\,v(u)^*\simeq v(u)^*\,e_*.$$
Thus the precomposition test for $v(u)$ at $z$ is a weak homotopy equivalence if and only if it is one at $vt$, by the component and homotopy-group argument of step 5. This reduction respects $q(z)\geq j$ because $q(z)=q(vt)=p(t)$.

source.place: Lemma B.2.4, proof (a), printed pp.1483-1484; agent expansion: extend the tests using equivalence edges, retaining their base labels

proof.text: If $u$ is $p$-cocartesian, step 4 makes its precomposition test invertible for every $t$ with $p(t)\geq j$. Step 5 gives the test for $v(u)$ at every such $vt$, and step 6 gives it at every $z$ with $q(z)\geq j$. Step 4 for $q$ now proves $v(u)$ is $q$-cocartesian. Conversely if $v(u)$ is $q$-cocartesian, its tests hold in particular at $vt$ for all $p(t)\geq j$; step 5 gives the tests for $u$, and step 4 for $p$ proves $u$ is $p$-cocartesian. This proves both implications for every edge, including edges over either identity of the interval.

source.place: Lemma B.2.4, proof (a), printed pp.1483-1484; agent expansion: assemble the two implications
